task.title: Add a source to a person
task.shortdesc: Describe a book, a register or a web page you used, so that someone else could find it again.

prereq.p: Open the page of Emily Brontë first. shows how.

context.p: A source is where you found something out. This page adds a source to Emily Brontë: a copy of the Haworth burial register that volunteers typed out.

step.cmd: Choose in the part that starts , then choose .

info.p: The list scrolls. Turn the mouse wheel with the pointer on it to find the part.

stepresult.p: A form opens. It starts with , which you can leave alone.

step.cmd: In , type the name of the source.

info.p: This box is needed. Say what you saw. For this source, type Haworth burial register (volunteer transcription).

step.cmd: In , type where to look in the source.

info.p: For this source, type Burials of December 1848.

step.cmd: Fill in the other boxes if you can, then choose .

info.p: The form has , and . You can leave them empty.

stepresult.p: The page of the person opens again. A line at the top says Sourced by and the title.

result.p: The source is now in your tree. It is attached to the whole record of the person, so every part of the person's page that has a chip now counts one source.
result.note: Good practice: cite what you actually saw. If you saw a copy that someone typed out, say so in the title.

postreq.p: To say which fact a source backs, add it to that fact instead. shows how. Next: .
